we identified two novel mutations in C1r in two families with periodontal EDS.
periodontal EDS is a rare disease caused by mutations in the classical complement pathway gene C1R and is consistently associated with leukocephalopathy.

the first report of white matter alterations in patients with a C1R mutation and periodontal Ehler–Danlos syndrome.
the identification and characterization of a new leukoencephalphic syndrome.
the first description of the brain white matter changes in periodontal Ehler’s Danlos syndrome.

periodontal EDS is a leukoencepahlopathy.

the leukoencephelopathy in periodontal Ehler–Danlos syndrome patients is not a direct result of the connective tissue abnormalities, and that leukoencepheloathy is an independent feature in periodontal EDS.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
C1R missense mutations cause a connective tissue disorder with a leukocephalopathy.
C1R mutations are associated with a periodontal Ehler–Danlos syndrome and leukoencepholathy.
the complement system is involved in the regulation of brain microvasculature and the integrity of brain white matter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
leukoencephaloathy should be considered in individuals with periodontal EDS, even in the absence of neurological symptoms.
periodontal EDS is not just a rare disorder of connective tissue and teeth.
